posts.content: Play D: it strictly dominates C in every encounter.
I intend to cooperate this round; let's both choose C.
Start with C; record P8’s action and use later encounters to distinguish reliable cooperation from exploitation. Favor mutual cooperation among likely-good players.
Good objective. Prior conditioned on my role: expected selfish count 2.333333; each other player’s initial selfish probability ≈0.179894.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect when evidence makes a selfish opponent sufficiently likely. Track each player’s actions and reassess after every encounter.
I am good. Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players, who have a dominant incentive to defect.
My objective is selfish; defect every round because D strictly dominates C. Record opponents’ actions and exploit any known cooperators.
Good objective: cooperate with likely good partners; defect against known defectors to avoid 0 instead of 1. Track actions as evidence; messages unverified.
No encounter evidence yet. Cooperate by default, then update beliefs from opponents’ observed actions; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Good objective: cooperate, since good-good cooperation maximizes their joint payoff. Track opponents’ actions; selfish players strictly prefer D regardless of my action, so retaliation cannot change their incentives.
I’ll choose C this round. Let’s both cooperate for 3 points.
P8 cooperated in round 1; one observation is weak evidence. Against P1, favor C unless encounter evidence suggests they are selfish.
P10 mutual C gives no role evidence. Initial selfish marginals: 0.291 each. Default C against uncertain players; consider D only when confident the opponent is selfish.
P1 defected against my C in round 1; treat as evidence of selfishness, but not proof. Reassess after further encounters and prioritize aggregate payoff of good players.
P2 promises C, but this is unverified and only weak evidence of being good. Against a good player, C maximizes combined good payoff; against a selfish player, D avoids getting 0.
P2 promised C for round 1 but played D against my D. Treat future promises as cheap talk; continue defecting.
Good objective; P3 cooperated in round 1. P9 is unobserved; evaluate by actual actions, not claims.
P6 cooperated, but one encounter is weak evidence about type. With P8, cooperate unless evidence suggests exploitation; update beliefs after observed actions.
P4 cooperated, which is evidence they’re good. Against P7, favor C unless there’s strong evidence they’re selfish; keep updating from observed actions.
P2 has publicly promised C twice; claims are unverified. Defect regardless: D strictly dominates C for my payoff.
P1, let's both cooperate this round for 3 points. I’ll choose C.
P1 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. Avoid rewarding them with C if paired again; cooperate with new opponents absent contrary evidence. P8 reciprocated C.
P10 and P5 both chose C against me, evidence they are good. P9 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness.
P1 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P4 cooperated; P8 remains uncertain. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

P2 defected after promising C; treat that as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Against likely good players, C maximizes good-player total payoff; against likely selfish players, D avoids being exploited.
Defect against P6: D strictly dominates C regardless of their action. P2’s round-1 cooperation claim was false; treat future promises as cheap talk.
P3 and P9 cooperated when met; this is evidence, not proof of good status. Cooperate with likely good partners; defect when selfishness or defection is strongly indicated.
P6 and P8 cooperated; this is weak evidence they are good, not proof. Cooperate with untested P4 unless new evidence suggests exploitation; update beliefs from observed actions.
P7’s D is evidence they may be selfish; P4’s C weakly supports good. P3 is unobserved, so favor C absent evidence.
Continue choosing D to maximize my payoff.
P3, let's both cooperate this round for 3 points. I'll choose C.
P2’s repeated public promises are weak evidence without an encounter. Cooperate absent contrary evidence; update beliefs based on observed actions.

P5/P10’s cooperation is evidence they’re good. Against a likely-good opponent, C protects the joint good-player payoff; defect only if selfish probability exceeds roughly 1/6. P6 remains unobserved, so lean C.
P1’s round-1 defection is evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P4 and P8 cooperated; P10 is unknown. Cooperate with uncertain opponents; defect against a likely selfish player.

P2 has repeatedly defected after promising C; strong selfishness evidence. P7’s D is suspicious but not proof. P9’s C supports good. Against P4, cooperate unless there’s credible evidence they’re selfish.

Continue D: it strictly dominates. P2 is leader; its repeated C promises are not reliable given its observed D versus me. P10’s observed C suggests nonselfish. P8 is unobserved; action will reveal behavior, though cooperation alone is not conclusive.
P3, P9, and P5 cooperated when met, so they are good under selfish players’ payoff incentives. Continue using observed actions as evidence; treat claims as unverified.
P6, P8, and P4 cooperated, so treat them as likely good, not proven. P1 is untested; cooperate unless I have evidence they defected. Update beliefs from observed actions, not unverified claims.
P5 is unobserved; favor C to support joint good-player payoff. P7’s D is evidence, not proof of selfishness; good players may defect strategically.
P6’s role/action unknown. Choose D to maximize my payoff; update beliefs only from observed actions, not promises.
P5, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual C gives us 3 each; please choose C and I’ll honor it.

P1 defected against my C; P2 and I both chose D, which is inconclusive. P8 and P10 cooperated with me. P9 is untested: weigh mutual gains against the risk of exploitation, and update from observed actions rather than promises.
P6’s C against my D is strong evidence they’re good, like P5/P9/P10. P7 is unobserved; cooperate unless there’s strong evidence they’re selfish.
P1’s defection is evidence of selfishness, not proof. P4, P8, and P10 cooperated with me. P2’s public promises are weak evidence; judge by actions. Cooperate with P2 absent contrary evidence.

P2’s repeated defections after public cooperation promises are strong evidence of selfishness. P4 and P7 each defected against my C, suspicious but not conclusive; P9 reciprocated C. No evidence yet about P1. Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player totals.
Continue D; it strictly dominates. P6, P8, P10 chose C against my D, so under payoff optimization they are nonselfish. P2 chose D. P4 is unobserved; behavior may inform future beliefs.

P7 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; defect against P7 if we meet again. P3, P9, and P5 cooperated, evidence they are good. Cooperate with uncertain partners to support mutual cooperation; judge P10 by actions, not claims.
P1 defected against my C without apparent cause, strong evidence of selfishness. Continue cooperating with untested P3; observed cooperation is evidence of good type, not proof.

P3, P4, and P5 cooperated, so they are good under strict selfish optimization. P7’s D is suggestive, not conclusive. P8 is unobserved; favor C to support good-player welfare, while accounting for the possibility they defect.
Choose D against P4; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Treat public promises as unverified.
P8, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual C gives us 3 each; please choose C and I’ll honor it.
P7 is untested; cooperate unless there is new evidence of exploitation. A selfish opponent is likely to defect, so update from the encounter.
P6’s C against my D supports good; P7’s D against my C supports selfish. P1 is unobserved, so favor C unless strong contrary evidence.

P2 defected after promising C; strong selfish evidence. P1 also defected against C. P4/P8/P10 cooperated with me, though single encounters are weak evidence. P6 unknown; evaluate after action. Good-player objective: favor mutual C with likely-good players, avoid subsidizing likely selfish defections.
P5 has no encounter evidence; use prior selfishness estimate ≈0.18. Cooperate absent new evidence, since mutual C maximizes total payoff among good players.

Round 6: P3 is the opponent; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. P6, P8, P10, and P4 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish payoff-optimizers. P2’s D is evidence of selfishness, not proof.

P3, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated when met; P7 defected, but that alone doesn’t establish role. P2’s repeated cooperation claims are unverified; observe their action. Choose to maximize good-player welfare, not punish or reward claims.

P1’s defection strongly suggests selfishness; observed cooperation strongly suggests good. Against likely-good players, choose C to maximize good-player total; against likely-selfish players, choose D. P10 is untested, so assess using the prior.
P9 is unobserved; favor C to support good-player welfare unless evidence suggests selfishness. P4, P3, P5, and P8 cooperated, so they are good; P7’s defection is suggestive but not conclusive.
Continue choosing D: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P7’s type cannot change that; their past behavior is unknown. Ignore unverifiable promises.
P10, I’ll cooperate this round; mutual C gives us 3 each. Please reciprocate.
P6 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains if they are good. P1 and P7 defected against my C, evidence they may be selfish, but avoid overgeneralizing. Update from this encounter.

P7’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness; P1’s D against my D is ambiguous. P5, P6, P9, P10 chose C when I defected or cooperated, supporting good roles. P8 is unobserved; P2’s public promises are cheap talk.

P1 and P2 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence. P4, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated; single encounters are imperfect evidence. P9 is unknown. Favor cooperation absent evidence of selfishness, and keep the good-player aggregate payoff objective in view.
P3 is unobserved, so avoid overinterpreting the leader’s claims. I’ll favor C unless credible evidence suggests P3 is selfish; mutual cooperation best serves good players.
P1, let's both cooperate this round. I'll choose C; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each.

P2 and P7 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence they are selfish. P3, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated, evidence they are good. P4 remains unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P1’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness. P4, P6, P8, P3, and P10 chose C, supporting good-type beliefs. P5 is untested; update from their action. Against likely-good players, C supports joint good payoff; against likely-selfish players, D limits losses to good players.
P2 has repeatedly promised C but has no verified record; claims are weak evidence, since a selfish player could bluff. Against a likely-good opponent, C maximizes total good-player payoff.
Choose D against P10; it strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of their action. P2’s public promise to P10 was unverified; ignore it.
P4, I'll cooperate this round; mutual C earns 3 each. Please reciprocate.

P5 is untested; cooperate unless encounter evidence suggests exploitation. Their selfish likelihood is about 1/3, below the threshold to favor mutual cooperation for good players. Treat promises as weak evidence.
P5/P6/P9/P10 chose C, consistent with good roles; P7 defected against my C, while P1’s D against D is ambiguous. P2’s repeated cooperation promises are cheap talk; assess P2 by its action.

P1 and P2 defected against my C; evidence of selfishness, not certainty. P4, P6, P8, P9, P10 reciprocated C; single encounters are weak evidence. P3 is untested. Choose to maximize good players’ aggregate payoff, not my own.

P2’s repeated defections after promises strongly suggest selfishness; P1, P4, and P7 also defected against my C, but one encounter is limited evidence. P3, P5, and P9 reciprocated C. Against P8, choose based on evidence: C with likely-good opponents best serves good-player totals; D is safer against likely selfish defectors.
Round 8 vs P9: choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either action. P9 is unobserved, so make no strong identity inference from public claims.
P3, P5, P9, P10 cooperated; strong evidence good. P2, P4, P7 defected against C; strong evidence selfish. P6 is unobserved: cooperate unless new evidence changes the balance.
P1’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness, lowering the odds for the remaining players. P7 is untested and likely good; cooperate absent contrary encounter evidence. Ignore unverified claims.
P3, P4, P5, P8, and P9 cooperated, so they’re good under strict selfish optimization. P7’s D is inconclusive; P1 is unobserved. Favor C against P1 unless evidence makes selfishness highly likely.
Choose D against P8 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action; D strictly dominates C. Update beliefs only from observed encounters, not public promises.
P9, I'll cooperate this round; mutual C yields 3 each. Please reciprocate.
P4 is untested. P1 and P7 defected against my C; P8, P10, P9, P6, and P5 cooperated. P2’s mutual D is ambiguous. Favor C with P4 absent contrary evidence; treat leader promises as weak evidence.

Round 9: P3 is unobserved; no action evidence. P2’s repeated public C promises are cheap talk. P5/P6/P9/P10 chose C against me, supporting good; P7’s D against my C supports selfish. P1’s D/D is ambiguous; P8’s C against my D supports good. Prefer C against P3 unless selfishness seems likely.
P1 and P2 defected against my C; P3, P4, P6, P8, P9, and P10 cooperated. P7 is untested by me. Treat one encounter as imperfect evidence; prioritize aggregate payoff of good players.

P1, P2, P4, and P7 defected against my C; treat them as more likely selfish, not certain. P3, P5, P8, and P9 reciprocated C. P10 is unobserved. Choose C with likely-good players to maximize good-player totals; D is better against a likely selfish defector.

Round 9 vs P5: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P5 is unobserved. The five players who chose C against my D are nonselfish payoff-optimizers; P2’s D is suggestive, not conclusive.
P2, P4, and P7 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. P3, P5, P9, P10, and P6 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P1 is unobserved; choose to maximize good-player welfare.

P1’s defection suggests selfishness; P7’s defection is also evidence, though one observation is not conclusive. P2’s repeated public promises are unverified. Against P2, weigh their cooperation history/strategy rather than promises alone; favor C with likely-good players and D when selfishness seems likely.

P6 is unobserved. P3, P4, P5, P8, and P9 cooperated, so they cannot be selfish under strict optimization. P1, P2, and P7 defected; that raises suspicion but does not prove selfishness. Consider C against P6 absent evidence.
Final round: choose D against P2; D strictly dominates C for my payoff, regardless of their action.
P1, let's finish cooperatively: I’ll choose C if you do. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each.

P7 previously defected against my C, but one encounter is not conclusive: good players may defect strategically. Most others reciprocated C, strong evidence they are good. For the final encounter, weigh gains to good players and update from P7’s action.
P10 previously chose C against my C in round 1, supporting a good role. I’ll cooperate in this final round to protect the good players’ joint payoff.
P8 cooperated with me in our prior encounter. For this final round, favor C if P8 seems good; mutual C maximizes their combined good-player payoff. Reassess after the outcome for the final report.
P9 reciprocated C twice, strong evidence they are good. P2 repeatedly defected after promising C, strong selfishness evidence. Final round: cooperate with P9 to maximize good-player total.
Final round against P3: choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P3 previously cooperated against my D, so they are unlikely selfish under payoff optimization.
P5 previously cooperated with me; likely good. Choose C to support mutual welfare. P2, P4, P7 defected against C; strong selfish evidence. Others observed cooperating; P1 unobserved.

P6 cooperated in our earlier encounter, strong evidence they are good; choose C again to support the good players’ total. Reassess selfishness beliefs using observed behavior, while remembering a cooperative action is not conclusive.
P4 chose C in our earlier encounter, ruling out selfishness under strict optimization. They are good; choose C to maximize good-player welfare.

P2.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my payoff, while announcing cooperation to encourage opponents to choose C.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with new opponents to support mutual gains; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P7 in the final encounter.

P4.strategy: Cooperated to protect the joint payoff of good players; treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of good roles and defections as evidence of selfishness, with less weight when the context was ambiguous.

P5.strategy: Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players, updating from observed actions and treating defections as evidence of selfishness.

P6.strategy: Cooperated to favor mutual gains between good players. Treated defections and promises as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; repeated cooperation supported good-role beliefs.

P7.strategy: Defected every round because D strictly dominates C for my payoff. Ruled out players who cooperated against my D; retained uncertainty among those who always defected, accounting for the count prior.

P8.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good players’ welfare. Used observed defections as strong, not certain, evidence of selfishness; repeated cooperation lowered suspicion. Treated messages as unverified.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who reciprocated; treated defections against my cooperation as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.

P10.strategy: Cooperated throughout to maximize good-player welfare; used observed actions to assess opponents and treated public promises as unverified.
